name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> with domain=chapter_event. The '43' is the dispatch index 0x43 in the per-event handler table @ 0x51B91 (entry @ 0x51C9D holds this fn's address 0x35A2F; neighbor 0x35A48 is index 0x44), a meaningful domain ID consistent with sibling handlers (handler_42, handler_44), NOT a Ghidra address residue (0x35A2F has no 43 tail). Descriptor accurately reflects behavior: 'unref' = no chapter FDFIELD turn-event/tile-step hook references this slot; 'dyn_turn_event' = arms a dynamic turn-event by writing the current turn counter into the hook table.
purpose: Chapter per-event dispatch handler (idx 0x43, currently unreferenced by any chapter hook): arm a dynamic turn-event for the current battle turn by writing the live turn counter into hook entry 1's turn byte of the tile-event data table.
logic_summary: Stack-frame __CHK(4) prologue (no real params consumed). Reads the global byte data_fd2_battle_turn_counter and stores it (as a single byte, no +1) into *(uint8*)(data_fd2_tile_event_data_table_ptr + 6) -- i.e. the turn byte of hook entry 1 in the tile-event data table. No consume-flag gate, so repeated calls keep overwriting the same slot. Disasm: MOV EAX,[tile_event_data_table_ptr]; MOV DL,byte ptr [turn_counter@0x53BEF]; MOV byte ptr [EAX+0x6],DL; RET -- the (uint8) truncation on store reproduces the 8-bit MOV exactly.

params.name: event_arg
params.semantics: Generic event argument supplied by the per-event dispatcher (table @ 0x51B91 signature is 1-arg cdecl void fn(uint event_arg)). This handler does not read it (cast to void); present only to match the uniform dispatch ABI.
params.reason: Conventional, accurate name for the dispatcher-supplied event argument; matches sibling handlers' parameter naming; no address residue.

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effect only: arms the dynamic turn-event slot.

notes: Writes a global (data_fd2_tile_event_data_table_ptr+6) but does not write a named global symbol directly (it dereferences the table pointer), hence writes_globals is empty; data_fd2_tile_event_data_table_ptr is read (the pointer load) and listed under reads_globals. Disassembly confirms the src comment exactly (MOV DL,[0x53BEF] / MOV [EAX+0x6],DL). Src comment block (chevt2.c lines 869-887) is already concise, accurate and ASCII-clean -> kept verbatim (no Edit). Ghidra plate is detailed, semantically consistent with src (same facts, more verbose) and non-contradictory -> left untouched (none). Both referenced global symbol names are established across globals.h and many .c files. No logic change (refine touches name-judgement + comments only).
